Flash video players for some reason refuse to obey by the rules of power management tools. Since it occurs on all platforms I assume it's a (stupid) conscious design choice. I recommend using mpv+youtube-dl to watch things on Youtube and Twitch. Just type in "mpv [link]" on the command line to launch a video.

If you access them from Firefox or a Firefork, the Open With addon allows you to quickly launch links with other applications. To set it up for mpv, flip all the options to "display as menu items", click on "Add...", navigate to /bin/ on your root partition (it may take a bit to load), and select mpv. Now when you want to watch a video, right click on a link or a tab and you can launch it in mpv.

Aside: Ironically I found this out with the opposite goal in mind. I wanted mpv to not pause the sleep timer so I could play something while I sleep but not have it run the whole night. I hacked together an alias that launches my file manager so I can pick out a video, wait two hours, and go to sleep.

alias sleepytime='spacefm && sleep 7200 && sudo pm-suspend'

Note: You need to edit sudoers so your user is in a group that has access to power. You still need to sudo but it doesn't ask for a password.

A couple of things to keep in mind when dealing with the AMD/fglrx driver (From a Radeon HD 6870 user who has some battle scars)

  • for an HTPC, once you get it working avoid updating the system and avoid any rolling release distro. It can blow your setup up.

  • What Kernel are you using? I have found, from a Debian point of view, that fglrx does not play well with any version of the kernel above the 3.16 (stable) version. I could not get Catalyst Control Center to even work with any stability with newer kernel versions.

  • There is a new version of the flash plugin for the Chrome/Chromium browser, if you are not using the latest update to the browser with the new flash plugin that might be worth checking out. (especially if you are using a different browser than Chrome. (Chromium is bad with flash, use Chrome)
